1.5.0.lead: Documents that belong together, an archive that adds up and takes several at once, a transfer code for the banking app, PDFs with a password, and an address through which somebody without an account sends you files.

sections.title: What goes together
sections.body: A delivery note belongs to its invoice. Under the notes of a document there is now the section “Goes with”: “Connect” finds the other document, and from then on both show each other. nexpaper also reads the numbers on a paper (invoice, order and delivery note number) from the text and from the data of an e-invoice, and proposes documents with the same number to each other, with the reason, at the document and as a line in the inbox. “Doesn't fit” puts a proposal away for good. Nothing is connected by itself, and two documents whose senders are both known and different are never proposed. You need to be able to edit both documents; “Disconnect” takes a connection back and deletes nothing.

sections.title: The archive adds up and takes several at once
sections.body: Under the table the archive now says what the amounts of the documents it found add up to, euros first, other currencies beside them, and how many have no amount. With “Select” every row gets a box, and the bar adds or removes a tag, sets the kind, moves to another vault, connects with each other or moves to the trash, for up to 500 documents at once. What you may not change is left out, and a line says how many and why. Moving and the trash ask first.

sections.title: Saved searches and pins
sections.body: “Save” keeps a search as it stands, with its words and filters, under a name in the side bar under “Saved”, with the number of hits beside it. Up to 30, yours alone, to rename, reorder and delete. A pin on a document puts it under “Pinned” at the top of the archive's overview and on the quick upload, up to 20, also yours alone.

sections.title: Transfer code for the banking app
sections.body: When a document names a recipient, an IBAN and an amount, there is now “Transfer”: a code (known as GiroCode) that your banking app scans, and the fields of the transfer fill themselves in. Every field says where it comes from: from the data of an e-invoice, or read from the text, which you then compare with the paper. With more than one IBAN in the document you choose one; the amount and the reference can be changed before you scan. nexpaper transfers nothing itself and stores nothing of it. “Mark as paid” ticks off the due date, if the document has one.

sections.title: A note on a sender, and the follow-up
sections.body: A sender can carry a note of up to 500 characters, say the customer number, the contract number or a phone number. It shows on every document of that sender in the vault; everybody in the vault sees it, nobody through a share of a single document. And a document can get a date “Follow up” with a sentence of what to do then. It stands on the Deadlines page and reminds you on the day itself at 8; the sentence is never part of the reminder.

sections.title: PDFs with a password
sections.body: A PDF that needs a password now waits in the inbox with a field for it. After “Open” nexpaper reads it like any other document. The original stays as it came, protected; beside it nexpaper keeps an opened copy without the password on the server, which the view, the search, the page tools, links and exports use. With “Remember for future documents” the password gets a name, and protected PDFs that you upload yourself later, or that come into your own vault through the intake folder or the mailbox, open by themselves. Up to 10 per person, never shown again, and nobody else's are ever tried.

sections.title: Links take along what goes with a document
sections.body: A link to the outside can now also show the documents that go with the one you share, but only those you tick when you make it and may share yourself; what comes to go with it later is not added. The export for the tax adviser can take along what goes with its documents (“Take the documents that go with them”). And whoever may change a document now sees that it is visible to the outside through a link, without to whom, and is asked before changing its pages, because the link shows the document as it is now.

sections.title: Ask for a document
sections.body: With “Ask for a document” you get an address that you give to somebody without an account, the tax office or the property manager, who drops files there. The files land in your inbox in your own vault, marked with the name you gave the request; nothing is filed by itself. A request lasts at most as long as a link, takes 10 files unless you say otherwise, and can be withdrawn at any time. The page behind the address shows who asks and how many files still go, never what has arrived. Off from the start: the operator switches upload requests on under Settings, Sharing, and they need the public address of the server.

sections.title: A mail's text as a document
sections.body: A mail without an attachment, such as a forwarded order confirmation, can now become a document: a PDF of its text in the inbox of the person who sent it, titled with the subject. Off from the start. Only for mails from a confirmed address of a person, and only when your mail server says the mail passed DMARC; never for unknown senders, and at most 50 a day per person.

small: Before the update: make a backup. nexpaper makes one itself before it changes the database, but after that no older version opens this database any more; the way back is only through the backup.
After the update nexpaper reads the numbers of the documents that are already there once, in the background. Proposals for older documents appear as it gets through them.
New search words: `linked:yes` and `pinned:yes`, and a filter “Follow up” on the Deadlines page.
Remembered PDF passwords are stored encrypted with the server key. A backup together with `secret.key` can open them, so keep backups protected.
“Ready for the internet?” has a point for upload requests, and the trial run of a restore names the links, upload requests and remembered PDF passwords that a restore would bring back.

For programs: `GET /api/v1/search/sum`, `POST /api/v1/documents/bulk`, `/api/v1/saved-searches`, `/api/v1/documents/{id}/related`, `/api/v1/documents/{id}/transfer`, `/api/v1/pins`, `/api/v1/pdf-passwords` and `/api/v1/upload-requests`. A document has the new fields `has_related`, `pinned`, `sender_memo` and `shown_outside`.

1.4.3.lead: No new feature this time, but news: nexpaper is now available as an app for iPhone and iPad.

sections.title: nexpaper on the App Store
sections.where: My account, Devices and apps, Pair a device
sections.body: With the app you scan letters with the camera, send PDFs and photos from other apps into your inbox through Share, file them, search the full text and keep an eye on your deadlines, with reminders if you like. Without a connection every scan waits on the device and uploads by itself once your server is reachable. The app is free and talks only to your own nexpaper. To connect it, show the QR code under “Pair a device” and scan it with the app, or sign in from the app through the browser.

sections.title: Android: testers wanted
sections.body: We would like to build an app for Android as well. Before Google lets a new app into the Play Store, it has to run in a closed test with 20 testers. If you have an Android device and would like to help, sign up in the discussion on GitHub.

link.label: Go to the discussion on GitHub

small: Nothing else changes, the database neither.

1.4.2.lead: A page the browser translated no longer takes nexpaper down.

sections.title: Pages the browser translated
sections.where: Every page, when Chrome, Edge or an extension translates it
sections.body: A translated page could go blank as soon as something on it changed, because the browser had swapped the texts for its own. nexpaper now keeps working on such a page.

1.4.1.lead: Deadlines can be switched off per person, “May go” is in the archive, and expired documents can go to the trash by themselves.

sections.title: Switch deadlines off per person
sections.body: If you do not use deadlines, switch them off there, for yourself. Then the menu has no Deadlines item and no number (on the phone the bar has Organise again), there are no reminders and no weekly overview, and the archive has no Deadline filter. The dates on the documents stay, only “paid” and “later” are gone for you; the search words with deadline: keep working. The others in the household are not affected. Deadlines are on from the start.

sections.title: “May go” in the archive
sections.body: The archive has a filter “May go”: the documents whose keeping time is over, as a table with the column “Keep until” and whether the date comes from the kind or was set by hand. With the boxes you choose what goes to the trash; nexpaper asks first, as always. When there is something to clear out, the overview of the archive says so in one line. The Deadlines page keeps its section.

sections.title: Expired ones into the trash by themselves
sections.body: Every kind with a keeping time has a switch “Put expired ones in the trash by themselves”, off from the start. When it is on, nexpaper puts the expired documents of the kind in the trash once a day, at night at 3 o'clock, at most 500 a day and each document only once; whoever restores one keeps it. That includes a date set by hand and documents you file later whose time is already over; the document page and the inbox say so under “Keep until”. Switching it on asks first and says how many documents it would affect right away (for a kind that applies to every vault the number counts only what you see). Nothing is deleted for good by it: they stay in the trash for 30 days. The history of the document, the weekly overview, a line in the archive overview and the trash say what nexpaper put away.

sections.title: Clearer what happens when the time is over
sections.body: The question for “N years” of keeping now always says what happens once the time is over: the document is in the archive under “May go” and nothing is deleted by itself, or nexpaper puts it in the trash by itself when the switch of the kind is on.

small: The update adds a column to the kinds (schema 14). nexpaper makes a backup itself first; going back to 1.4.0 works only through that backup.

1.4.0.lead: Deadlines on a page of their own, reminders for invoices, cancellations and warranties, and a keeping time for every kind.

sections.title: Deadlines in one place
sections.body: The menu now has Deadlines, between Archive and Vaults, with the number for the next 14 days. The page shows what has to be paid, cancelled or claimed under a warranty, from all vaults where you may edit: what is overdue, the next two weeks, and what comes later. A deadline can be marked as done (paid, cancelled) and opened again, or put off with “Later” for you alone to tomorrow, in three days or in a week. For a contract you enter the notice period and the renewal: nexpaper works out the last day to cancel and shows it beside the field, and without a cancellation “Contract until” moves on by itself after it has run out. When a cancellation has to arrive is written in the contract; nexpaper only does the sums.

sections.title: Reminders by push and mail
sections.body: nexpaper now reminds you in good time: of an invoice that falls due three days ahead, of the last day to cancel 14 days ahead, of a warranty that runs out 30 days ahead, each once more on the day itself, at 8 in the morning in your time zone. How early, whether by push to the phone or by mail, whether one by one, once a week or both, you set under My account, Reminders. There you can also mute single vaults, and a test message shows that everything arrives. The weekly overview comes on Mondays at 8 by mail and only when something is coming up. Everybody who may edit in the vault is reminded; somebody who only reads gets nothing. The message holds the kind, the date and the title of the document, never the amount, the text or the notes. From the start, reminders come one by one by push; mail and the weekly overview are off.

sections.title: Keeping times for kinds
sections.body: Every kind can get a keeping time in years, in the column “Keep”. The kinds of the server are kept by the operator, those of a vault by whoever manages it. From the start no kind has one. Years are counted from the end of the year in the document date, and nexpaper asks whether the time should also apply to the documents that are already there; what was set by hand stays. When the time is over, the document appears on the Deadlines page under “May go”. nexpaper never deletes by itself: you choose what goes to the trash, where it stays for another 30 days. The usual times it names are a help without guarantee and no legal advice.

small: Before the update: make a backup. nexpaper makes one itself before it changes the database, but after that no older version opens this database any more; the way back is only through the backup.

Deadlines that are already entered cause no flood of reminders at the first start: what was inside its lead before is not reminded again, the day itself is still announced. A “Keep until” that exists already counts as set by hand.

New search words: `deadline:open`, `deadline:overdue`, `deadline:<30` (the next open deadline in less than 30 days) and `keep:expired`, plus a “Deadline” filter in the archive. The export for the tax adviser names the deadlines and “Keep until” in its list.

For programs: `GET /api/v1/deadlines`, the keeping time of kinds under `/api/v1/kinds/{id}/keeping` and the settings under `/api/v1/me/reminders`. `GET /api/v1/dashboard` also names the last day to cancel as `notice` and leaves out what is done.

1.3.0.lead: Titles that say more, your own instructions for the AI, and an intake folder that may lie anywhere in the container.

sections.title: AI titles that tell a document apart
sections.body: The AI now proposes titles that say what the document is and what is particular to it, such as “Invoice 110526 – Tyres” instead of just “Invoice”: with the number of an invoice, a contract or a policy and what it is about, as far as the text names them. Nothing is made up.

sections.title: Your own instructions for the AI
sections.body: As the operator you can give the AI additional instructions, for example how your titles should look or in which language. They are added to the fixed rules and change nothing in which fields the AI fills and what nexpaper checks. Left empty, everything stays as it was.

sections.title: An intake folder wherever it is mounted
sections.body: In the container nexpaper took only /data/eingang as the intake folder; any other path was refused, a mounted one like /scans too. Now any mounted folder will do that does not lie in the program, in the data or in a system folder.

1.2.1.lead: A fix for the new archive.

sections.title: Whole titles in the table
sections.body: On a laptop the archive's table cut the titles short after a few words, because the other columns had fixed widths. Now title and sender share the room, the title gets twice as much.

1.2.0.lead: The archive stays easy to find your way in, with thousands of documents too.

sections.title: An overview as the way into the archive
sections.body: Without a search or a filter the archive now shows the newest documents and, below them, how everything spreads: by sender, by kind and by year, each with the number of documents, and the most frequent tags. A click on an entry shows exactly those documents. Behind “All senders” is the whole list with a search field.

sections.title: A table with pages instead of an endless list
sections.where: Archive, “Show all”, a search or a filter
sections.body: What is found stands in a table with numbered pages, 25, 50 or 100 a page. A click on title, sender, date or amount sorts by it, a second click turns the order around. The page, the order and the filters are in the address: a bookmark leads back to exactly there, and the back button of the browser leads to the overview.

small: The archive's filter has “Year” instead of “Time”, with the years there are documents from.
For programs: the search of the API takes `page` and `sort` too, and `GET /api/v1/search/overview` gives the numbers of the overview. The cursor stays.

1.1.2.lead: Two fixes: HDR photos from an iPhone and very large mailboxes.

sections.title: HDR photos from an iPhone make one page
sections.body: An HDR photo from an iPhone is a JPEG with a second, small picture behind it, the gain map. Until now it became a PDF of two pages, the second small and grey. Now only the photo becomes the page. As a profile picture such a photo was refused so far; now it is taken.

sections.title: Very large mailboxes as an input
sections.body: With a mailbox of well over 100,000 mails as the input, fetching stopped at the same place on every run after the first pass. The server sent the list of all mails in one line, and that line was longer than nexpaper would read. Now nexpaper asks for the newest mail alone and reads long answers too.

1.1.1.lead: A small fix for running behind a reverse proxy and for the language of the browser.

sections.title: X-Forwarded-Proto only from trusted proxies
sections.where: Settings, Sign-in, Ready for the internet?
sections.body: Whether cookies get the Secure flag and whether “Ready for the internet?” shows https as fine now depends only on a proxy listed in NEXPAPER_TRUSTED_PROXIES. Until now the X-Forwarded-Proto header of any sender counted for this. If nexpaper runs behind a proxy, list it there or set NEXPAPER_COOKIE_SECURE to on; otherwise cookies in auto mode stay without Secure.

small: The language of the browser is read the same way everywhere, also for new accounts and pushes: every weight counts, wherever it stands and however it is written
The https hint in “Ready for the internet?” names NEXPAPER_TRUSTED_PROXIES

1.1.0.lead: Sign in through several providers, as in every nex app: authentik, Microsoft Entra ID or any other that speaks OpenID Connect.

sections.title: Several sign-in providers
sections.body: Each provider gets a button on the sign-in page, in the order of your list. Per provider you choose whether new people get an account and whether it checks the second factor itself. Microsoft Entra ID works with several tenants too.

sections.title: authentik in one step
sections.body: With an API token nexpaper sets up provider and application in authentik itself and says for each step what worked and what did not. Who would rather not hand out a token downloads a blueprint instead.

sections.title: Linking in your account
sections.body: Every account links itself to the providers, with your password as confirmation, and undoes the link there. A mail address from the provider no longer links anything by itself; an invitation works through the provider too.

small: Your provider so far is the first entry of the list, every link stays, its redirect address too
An address from the provider counts for documents by mail only once you confirmed it, also one 1.0.1 took over as confirmed: confirm it once under My account, Profile
Behind a proxy nexpaper trusts, the scheme it reports counts too

“Require a second factor” is for signing in with a password: an account without a password, and whoever comes in through a provider whose entry has “The provider checks the second factor itself” on, is not made to set one up; the hints say so
A dashboard card can read nexpaper through an API key: what waits in the inbox, what is filed, and what falls due in the next 14 days.
Texts corrected: what API keys may do, when a push comes, how long a sign-in lasts and how the files on the disk are named
Forgot your password and no mail server: the command python -m app.reset_link in the container prints a link to set a new one, valid once and for 24 hours (see the README)
The shortcuts on the app symbol speak the language of your browser

1.0.1.lead: A small version: nexpaper now says more clearly where it is best kept.

sections.title: Best kept at home
sections.body: Your papers are best kept in your own network, and from on the way you come in through a VPN. The texts about the API no longer promise apps that are still to come.

small: The README and the security notes say the same

1.0.0.lead: This is nexpaper 1.0, a filing cabinet for documents at home and in a small business: the simple Paperless-ngx for the home. This is what you find from the start.

sections.title: Everything comes into the inbox first
sections.body: From the phone, the mailbox, the intake folder, Paperless or the browser: new files wait in the inbox with the fields filled in. Filter by vault, search the text too, look at every page large, and file many at once.

sections.title: Vaults
sections.body: Everybody has a vault of their own, and there are shared ones like “Household”. Sharing is read, edit or manage, and single documents can go out as a link.

sections.title: Organise
sections.body: Senders, kinds and tags in one place, with how many documents each has: rename, merge or delete them. Typing a sender or a tag proposes the ones you already have.

sections.title: Text recognition and search
sections.body: Scans become searchable PDFs and the original stays as it came. The search understands parts of words and filters like “kind:”, “sender:” and “amount:>”.

sections.title: Photographing with edge detection
sections.body: The camera finds the sheet, takes the picture by itself and straightens it. Several pages become one document.

sections.title: Pages and versions
sections.body: Turn, delete and order pages, join documents or split them at blank separator sheets. Every change is saved as a version of the document, the original stays.

sections.title: Backup and checking the files
sections.body: The backup holds the database, the settings and the server secrets, not the documents and not the search index. Once a week nexpaper checks the checksums of all files and warns at the document when one is missing or has changed.

small: E-invoices (ZUGFeRD, Factur-X, XRechnung) are read from their data
Kinds of their own per vault, and rules that help with filing
An export for the tax adviser as a ZIP, as a link if you like
Import from Paperless-ngx
From the iPhone with a shortcut, from Android through Share
A second factor, passkeys and sign-in through your own provider
